newsitem.title: MEXICO: Cemex plays down U.S. cement ruling.
newsitem.headline: Cemex plays down U.S. cement ruling.

text.p: Mexican cement industry leader Cementos Mexicanos (Cemex) on Tuesday played down new U.S. dumping duties that levy tariffs of up to 109.85 percent on Mexican cement imported between 1993 and 1995.

"The United States is a market but it's not the belly button of the world. There are other markets as good and as important...Asia in particular," said Javier Prieto, a vice president of trading at the company.
On April 4, the U.S. Department of Commerce said the affected Mexican cement companies would have to pay duties retroactively for shipments imported to the United States during 1993-1995.
"We are not scared but neither are we crossing our arms," Prieto told reporters after an export conference. "We're fighting and competing".
He said exports were expected to continue around four million tonnes in 1997, their approximate level last year.
